option_relations.rationale: The patient's symptoms of tingling pain in the sole of his right foot when raising it above chest level, calf cramps, and absent pedal pulses are consistent with peripheral artery disease (PAD).
Intermittent claudication is a symptom of peripheral artery disease (PAD).
The patient's symptoms do not suggest lumbar spinal stenosis, as there is no pain in the back and muscle strength is normal.
While the patient has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, the symptoms described are not typical of peripheral neuropathy.
